title: Enable DualShock 4 enhanced mode without changing your mappings
summary: Use SDL and enhanced mode only for a supported official controller, then test LEDs and vibration separately.

Enable DualShock 4 enhanced mode without changing your mappings

blocks.text: PCSX2 documents an enhanced mode for official DualShock 4 and DualSense controllers. It adds LED control and helps vibration motors work correctly; it does not add these hardware features to third-party controllers. This is separate from ordinary button mapping. Start from SDL, the recommended cross-platform source, and change one option at a time.

Use an official Sony controller and a reliable USB or Bluetooth connection. Close the game, note the input source and current vibration mappings, and record whether the controller is wired. If it is a third-party lookalike, leave enhanced mode off. Keep a known menu or test utility ready so you can verify input without risking a save.

items: 1. Open Settings > Controllers and select SDL.
2. Confirm the DS4 or DualSense appears as the active SDL device. Do not change to XInput or DirectInput during this test.
3. Enable DualShock 4 / DualSense Enhanced Mode in the SDL section.
4. Use the lightbulb control beside SDL only to test the LED; keep the existing color if this is not needed.
5. Open Controller Port 1 and verify the button and stick mappings remain present.
6. Test button input in a safe menu, then trigger known in-game rumble if you also need to validate motors.

blocks.text: Pass when buttons and sticks still reach the expected PS2 controls. For optional extras, confirm the LED changes only through its lightbulb control and that a known rumble event reaches the controller. A checked option alone does not prove vibration: transport, operating-system permissions, motor mapping, and the game itself can affect it.

items: Mode has no effect: confirm this is an official DS4/DualSense selected through SDL.
Buttons work but vibration does not: verify the game requests rumble and inspect the Large Motor and Small Motor entries for the active source.
LED control is present but no change occurs: reconnect the controller and test once more.
All controls disappeared: restore the recorded source and reselect the device before remapping.

blocks.text: Close emulation, disable enhanced mode, and restore the recorded source and motor mappings. Reopen the same menu and confirm ordinary buttons work. If only LED or rumble fails, leave regular mappings intact and troubleshoot that feature on its own; clearing all mappings will not repair a connection or motor fault.
